title: Bounded-above resolutions from a quotient-generating class
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $\mathcal P\subset\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal A)$ contain a zero object, and assume every object of $\mathcal A$ is a quotient of an object of $\mathcal P$. Let $a\in\mathbf Z$. If $K^\bullet$ is a cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with $K^n=0$ for every $n>a$, then there exist a cochain complex $P^\bullet$ and a quasi-isomorphism $P^\bullet\to K^\bullet$ such that every $P^n$ lies in $\mathcal P$, every component $P^n\to K^n$ is an epimorphism, and $P^n=0$ for every $n>a$.

proof.text: Put $Z^jK=\ker d_K^j$. For an integer $n\le a+1$, the induction data consist of objects $P^j\in\mathcal P$, maps $\alpha^j:P^j\twoheadrightarrow K^j$ and differentials $d_P^j$ for $j\ge n$, with $P^j=0$ for $j>a$, $d_P^{j+1}d_P^j=0$ and $\alpha^{j+1}d_P^j=d_K^j\alpha^j$. Require also that the induced cycle map $u_n:Z^nP\to Z^nK$ is epic, and that the induced maps $Z^jP/\operatorname{im}d_P^{j-1}\to H^j(K)$ are isomorphisms for $j>n$. These quotients involve only the already specified degrees. At $n=a+1$, choose in every degree above $a$ the zero object belonging to $\mathcal P$, with zero maps. All corresponding terms of $K$, cycles and cohomology in the required degrees vanish, so the requirements hold.

Assume the data at $n$ have been chosen. Form $T_n=K^{n-1}\times_{Z^nK}Z^nP$, where the first map is the factorization of $d_K^{n-1}$ through $Z^nK$, and the second is $u_n$. Explicitly, $T_n$ is the kernel of $(\overline d_K^{n-1},-u_n):K^{n-1}\oplus Z^nP\to Z^nK$, so it exists using kernels and a finite biproduct. Write its projections as $s:T_n\to K^{n-1}$ and $t:T_n\to Z^nP$. The quotient-generating hypothesis supplies $Q\in\mathcal P$ and an epimorphism $q:Q\twoheadrightarrow T_n$. Set $P^{n-1}=Q$, $\alpha^{n-1}=sq$, and $d_P^{n-1}=\iota_n tq$, with $\iota_n:Z^nP\to P^n$ the kernel inclusion. The kernel equation gives $\alpha^nd_P^{n-1}=d_K^{n-1}\alpha^{n-1}$, and $d_P^nd_P^{n-1}=0$ follows from $d_P^n\iota_n=0$. No previously chosen data are changed.

The new component $\alpha^{n-1}$ is epic. Indeed take any morphism $x:V\to K^{n-1}$. Since $u_n$ is epic, [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](a) gives an epimorphism $\rho:V'\twoheadrightarrow V$ and $z:V'\to Z^nP$ with $u_nz=\overline d_K^{n-1}x\rho$. The pair $(x\rho,z)$ defines a morphism $V'\to T_n$ by the kernel universal property. Apply the same criterion to $q$ to lift this morphism to $p:V''\to P^{n-1}$ after another epimorphism $\sigma:V''\twoheadrightarrow V'$. Then $\alpha^{n-1}p=x\rho\sigma$. Composites of epimorphisms are epimorphisms by right cancellation, so criterion (a) proves the claim.

The new cycle map $u_{n-1}:Z^{n-1}P\to Z^{n-1}K$ is epic. For any $x:V\to Z^{n-1}K$, the pair $(\iota_Kx,0)$ defines a morphism $V\to T_n$, because $d_K^{n-1}\iota_K=0$. By [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](a) for $q$, after an epimorphism $\rho:V'\twoheadrightarrow V$ this pair lifts to $p:V'\to P^{n-1}$. Its second component is zero, hence $d_P^{n-1}p=0$ and $p$ factors through $Z^{n-1}P$. Its first component gives $u_{n-1}\overline p=x\rho$, after cancelling the monic cycle inclusion. Criterion (a) now proves the assertion.

Write $h_n:H^n(P)\to H^n(K)$ for the map now defined by adjoining degree $n-1$. It is epic. The quotient $\pi_K:Z^nK\twoheadrightarrow H^n(K)$ is a cokernel, hence an epimorphism in an abelian category. Given $y:V\to H^n(K)$, [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](a) first lifts $y$ through $\pi_K$ after an epimorphic refinement, and then lifts the resulting cycle through the epic map $u_n$ after a second refinement. If $z:V'\to Z^nP$ is the final lift and $\rho:V'\twoheadrightarrow V$ the composite refinement, functoriality of the cohomology quotient gives $h_n\pi_Pz=y\rho$. Criterion (a) applied to $h_n$ proves epimorphy.

The map $h_n$ is also monic. Take $y:V\to H^n(P)$ with $h_ny=0$. Lift $y$ through the cokernel $\pi_P:Z^nP\twoheadrightarrow H^n(P)$ using [lem-sp-abelian-refinements](a): $\pi_Pz=y\rho$ for an epimorphism $\rho:V'\twoheadrightarrow V$. Then $\pi_Ku_nz=0$. Criterion (c), applied to the cokernel of $\overline d_K^{n-1}:K^{n-1}\to Z^nK$, gives an epimorphism $\sigma:V''\twoheadrightarrow V'$ and $b:V''\to K^{n-1}$ with $\overline d_K^{n-1}b=u_nz\sigma$. Thus $(b,z\sigma)$ maps to $T_n$. Lift it through $q$ after an epimorphism $\tau:V'''\twoheadrightarrow V''$, obtaining $p$ with $tqp=z\sigma\tau$. Consequently $z\sigma\tau$ is a boundary in $P$, so $y\rho\sigma\tau=\pi_Pz\sigma\tau=0$. Cancel these epimorphisms to get $y=0$. For two morphisms with equal composites with $h_n$, apply this to their difference; thus $h_n$ is monic. By step 5 and the abelian-category definition, $h_n$ is a cokernel of some morphism $v$. Since $h_nv=0$ and $h_n$ is monic, $v=0$. A cokernel of zero is an isomorphism by its universal property, so $h_n$ is an isomorphism.

Steps 2--6 establish the induction data at $n-1$: they give the new component epimorphism, new cycle epimorphism and the required cohomology isomorphism in degree $n$. For $j>n$, neither $P^{j-1}$, $P^j$, $P^{j+1}$ nor their maps were changed, so their quotient cohomology maps remain the previous isomorphisms. Recurse on $k\in\mathbf N$ with $n=a+1-k$, choosing one covering epimorphism at each step. Every integer degree is reached; once a term, differential or component is assigned it is retained. Hence these data define an actual cochain complex and a morphism $\alpha:P\to K$, with terms in $\mathcal P$, with every component epic, and with zero terms above $a$. For any fixed $j\le a$, the stage with lower endpoint $j-1$ establishes that $H^j(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism, and later stages leave it unchanged. For $j>a$ both cohomology objects vanish. Thus $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism by definition.

lean.statement: theorem exists_subcategory_left_resolution {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] (P : C → Prop) (hzero : ∃ Z : C, P Z ∧ IsZero Z) (hcover : ∀ X : C, ∃ (Y : C) (p : Y ⟶ X), P Y ∧ Epi p) (a : ℤ) (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, a < n → IsZero (K.X n)) : ∃ (L : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : L ⟶ K), QuasiIso f ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, P (L.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Epi (f.f n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, a < n → IsZero (L.X n))
